derived: This is a DERIVED benchmark. Every candidate was rewritten by a model. It is not untouched ResearchBench and must not be described as such.

diagnostic_verdict.bar_provenance: the frozen protocol said 'near 0.5' and 'substantially below 0.870' with no number; this bar was set explicitly by the research owner after that omission came to light
diagnostic_verdict.judge_noise_note: the question-hidden judge scored 0.870 and 0.890 on two runs over the same 100 official v2 pairs; ~0.02 is noise

decomposition.reading: canonicalisation cut the FRACTION of pairs carrying a usable text-only cue from 0.86 (v2) to 0.38, while leaving the cue nearly as strong on the pairs that still have one (0.977 -> 0.875)

question_hidden_judge_counterbalanced.note: Supersedes the single-order 0.686. Every pair judged in both orders and averaged, so position preference cancels exactly; a pure position-guesser scores 0.500 under this scheme.

gates: inherited R1/R3/R5/R6 row screen + R4 cutoff (reused verbatim from the v2 build)
symmetric canonicalisation, blind to candidate role
semantic preservation check on every canonical claim
R2 pair comparability re-applied to the CANONICAL texts
name: ResearchBench-derived canonicalized evaluation benchmark
no_length_gate: Length is measured and reported, never filtered. If a length cue survives canonicalisation that is a finding about the transformation.
not_used_in_construction: knowledge of which candidate is the gold, at any transformation step
screening_order: SHA256(DOI) ascending after DOI deduplication (v1 order)
status: EVALUATION CANDIDATE — FAILED the frozen style diagnostics; NOT usable as an evaluation benchmark
status_note: Diagnostics run after freezing: shortest-text-first 0.605, longest-text-first 0.395, question-hidden judge 0.643 counterbalanced (0.686 single-order, which was confounded by an 81% preference for option A). All three are outside a within-0.1-of-chance band, so the slice does not clear the bar it was built to clear. It remains a useful measurement of what symmetric canonicalisation can remove: the share of pairs with a detectable text-only cue fell from 86% to 38%, and semantic preservation was 94.8%. It may be used for development, but aggregate accuracy on it must not be reported as evidence for the method. See benchmark/canonical/canonical_report.md and docs/DECISIONS.md #16 and #21.
